In an at-risk patient (cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis B, prior hepatocellular carcinoma), hepatocellular carcinoma is diagnosed by imaging, without biopsy, when the LI-RADS major criteria are present: non-rim arterial phase hyperenhancement (APHE), non-peripheral washout, enhancing capsule, size and growth. An observation ≥ 20 mm with APHE and at least one other criterion is LR-5.
APHE is assessed in the LATE arterial phase (hepatic artery full, portal vein beginning to opacify). In this exam the arterial phase is early: the aorta is very dense but the portal vein and parenchyma are not yet enhanced, so the lesion's enhancement appears modest. This is a common technical error: with an early arterial phase a hepatocellular carcinoma may not show APHE and the LI-RADS category is downgraded.
The multinodular "mosaic" appearance (confluent nodules separated by septa) is typical of large hepatocellular carcinoma. Differential diagnosis: hemangioma fills in from the periphery and remains iso/hyperdense; focal nodular hyperplasia has no washout; hypovascular metastases have a peripheral rim in the arterial phase.
In the report: number and location of nodules (segments), diameter, relationship with the hepatic veins and portal vein (tumor thrombosis), signs of chronic liver disease and portal hypertension.
L'APHE si giudica in fase tardo-arterios: APHE is judged in the late arterial phase: with an early arterial phase, hepatocellular carcinoma may look hypovascular.
